question: My laptop won't connect to the VPN when I'm working from home
correctAnswerMustCover: Download/install the VPN client from the IT self-service page and sign in with institutional credentials
Approve the MFA prompt on your phone
A connect-then-disconnect pattern after a few seconds usually means an unapproved MFA prompt
answer:
You've tried connecting to the VPN and it keeps disconnecting after a few seconds. This might be due to an unapproved MFA prompt on your phone. Check if you have any notifications or prompts that require you to approve something, as this could be causing the issue.

If you're still having trouble, try mapping shared drives again while the VPN is active. Since mapped drives created on campus don't always reconnect automatically from home, it's possible that they need to be re-mapped manually.

Also, make sure you have administrator rights on your computer before attempting to install any software or connect to the VPN. If you're using a personally owned laptop, try using an administrator account; if you're on a campus computer, raise a Software ticket instead of trying to work around it.

sources.title: Connect to the VPN for off-campus access

question: How do I reset my password?
correctAnswerMustCover: Use 'Forgot password' on the sign-in page with your institutional email
The reset link is valid for 30 minutes
Password must be at least 12 characters with upper/lower case, a number and a symbol
answer:
To reset your password, follow these steps:

1. Open the sign-in page and select **Forgot password**.
2. Enter your institutional email address - personal email addresses won't be accepted.
3. Check your inbox for a reset link that's valid for 30 minutes.
4. Choose a new password that meets the password rules.
5. Sign in with the new password.

You can do this at any time, as it's a self-service option.

question: I've been locked out after typing my password wrong too many times
correctAnswerMustCover: Locks after 10 failed attempts within 15 minutes and clears itself after 30 minutes
Sign out of all devices (a saved old password on a phone/tablet re-triggers the lock)
Raise an Account ticket only if it keeps relocking within minutes
answer:
You're locked out because you entered your password incorrectly too many times. The most common cause is that there's an old password stored on another device, like a phone or tablet, that keeps trying to sign in automatically. Check all your devices that are signed into your email.

To fix this, follow these steps:

1. Sign out of your account on every phone, tablet, and personal computer you own.
2. Wait 30 minutes for the lock to clear.
3. Try signing in once on a single device and confirm it works.
4. Then sign back in on your other devices one at a time.

This should help you regain access to your account.

sources.title: Account locked after too many failed sign-in attempts

question: How do I set up two-factor authentication on my account?
correctAnswerMustCover: Install Microsoft Authenticator and add it as a sign-in method via account security settings
Scan the QR code and approve the test notification
Register a backup method in case the phone is lost
answer:
To set up multi-factor authentication (MFA) on your account, follow these steps:

First, install Microsoft Authenticator on your phone from the App Store or Google Play. Then, sign in to your account security settings on a computer and select **Add sign-in method**. Choose the authenticator app as the new sign-in method.

Next, scan the QR code shown on the computer screen using the app. After that, approve the test notification that appears on your phone.

question: I lost my student ID card, what should I do?
correctAnswerMustCover: Raise an Account ticket or visit the Help Desk immediately so the old card is deactivated
Replacement issued at the Help Desk with photo ID
First replacement each year is free; later ones carry a small fee
answer:
You should report the loss of your student ID card as soon as possible. Go to the Help Desk in person or raise a ticket under the Account category. 

[Note: You don't need to bring photo identification at this stage.]

question: The wifi in the library keeps dropping out
correctAnswerMustCover: Move closer to the centre of the room / check if others nearby have the same issue
Laptop power-saving settings can turn off the wireless adapter on battery -- check Device Manager power management
If it persists across days/locations, raise a Network ticket with building, room, time and device details
answer:
To help resolve the issue with the Wi-Fi in the library, let's start by checking if the connection stabilises when moving closer to the centre of the room. This can be affected by concrete walls, lift shafts, and metal shelving which weaken the signal.

Next, see if other people around you are experiencing the same problem at the same time. If they're not, it might be an issue with your device.

sources.title: Wi-Fi keeps dropping or is very slow
sources.section: What to include in a ticket

question: My print job isn't coming out of the printer
correctAnswerMustCover: Check the printer's own display panel first for a jam/empty tray/toner warning
Clear the stalled print queue and cancel any Error/Deleting jobs, then send a test page
Confirm the correct printer was selected, not a previously-used default in another building
answer:
Check the printer's display panel before doing anything on your computer to see if there are any error messages or warnings that might be stopping the print job. If you find a message, try clearing it as this may release every queued job at once.

If the issue persists, go to a campus multifunction device and tap your ID card to view your held jobs. Check which printer was selected for the print job and confirm the name matches the label on the physical device.

question: How do I top up my print credit?
correctAnswerMustCover: Top-ups are made online through the student portal
Balance is shown on the device screen after signing in, or on the self-service printing page
Credit can take up to 10 minutes to appear at the device
answer: To top up your print credit, go to the IT self-service site and log in with your student credentials. Then, click on "Print" and select "Top-up Print Credit". Follow the online instructions to complete the payment process. Alternatively, you can also check your remaining balance on the device screen after signing in.

question: Can I install Microsoft Office on my own personal laptop?
correctAnswerMustCover: Yes, Microsoft 365 is included, covering up to 5 computers and 5 mobile devices
Install from the Microsoft 365 portal and sign in with your institutional account so the licence activates
Uninstall any existing personal Office copy first to avoid activation conflicts
answer:
You can install Microsoft 365 on your personal laptop. However, you need to uninstall any existing personal version of Office first. This is because two versions of Office on one computer can cause activation conflicts. 

To do this, follow the steps in [2] Install Microsoft 365 on a personal device — Installing.

question: I think I received a phishing email, what should I do?
correctAnswerMustCover: Do not click links or reply; use the Report button in Outlook
IT will never ask for your password by email
If you already clicked/entered details, change your password immediately and raise an urgent Account ticket
answer: If you think you've received a phishing email, don't click any links or reply. Instead, use the Report button in Outlook to send the message for analysis and remove it from your mailbox. If the Report button is unavailable, forward the message to the Help Desk (our team) and then delete it.

sources.title: Recognise and report a phishing email

question: My OneDrive files aren't syncing anymore
correctAnswerMustCover: Check the cloud icon status (red cross = stopped, pause symbol = paused) and read the message it gives
Confirm you're still signed in and that you haven't run out of storage quota
Quit and reopen OneDrive to restart the sync before trying a full sign-out
answer: You've checked that you're signed in to your account, but your files still aren't syncing. Let's try restarting the sync. Quit OneDrive from the icon menu, then reopen it from the Start menu or Applications folder. This should resolve most stalls and get your files syncing again. If this doesn't work, we can explore other options together.

question: How long should it take for my ticket to get sorted out?
correctAnswerMustCover: Response targets depend on priority: Critical 4h, High 8h, Medium 24h, Low 72h, Trivial 120h
Targets are measured to resolution, not first response
Priority is set by impact, not by how urgently the ticket is worded
answer:
You've submitted a new ticket. The priority level you choose will affect how quickly we respond. 

Critical issues are usually resolved within 4 hours, High issues within 8 hours, Medium issues within 24 hours, Low issues within 72 hours, and Trivial issues default to 120 hours.

If your issue is not time-critical, waiting for the lockout period to expire (30 minutes) might be faster than raising a ticket.
